name: Ken Paxton
role: Texas Attorney General (since 2015); Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in 2026
summary: Ken Paxton is a hard-right Republican who served in the Texas House (2003-2013) and Senate (2013-2015) before becoming attorney general. He has used the office to bring suits against Obama and Biden policies on immigration, climate rules, healthcare, guns and LGBT issues, to enforce bans on abortion, gender transition care and DEI, and to pursue Big Tech on privacy and antitrust grounds. He is a Trump ally who won the 2026 Senate nomination and campaigns on border enforcement, tax deductions and America First policy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Led a 20-state suit to have the Affordable Care Act struck down entirely, said it should be replaced by a market plan of "better choices", and campaigns on tax deductions for out-of-pocket medical costs rather than a state guarantee.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Sued over the overtime rule; no stated position on the minimum wage.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Said on air "I am totally free market" and called court-ordered school finance redistribution "socialism"; qualifies this with support for antitrust action against dominant firms.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Called Texas school-finance redistribution "crushing the top" socialism, attacks his opponent for votes for income and estate taxes, and campaigns on tax cuts.

unions-good.rationale: Opposing compulsory dues and release time is nearby; he did not state a view on unions as such.

property-fundamental.rationale: Filed a Takings Clause amicus brief arguing governments must pay compensation for property taken, and sued over Biden-era removal of Texas border barrier as destruction of state property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Pursues Big Tech, pharma, food and asset-manager suits, but pledges to remove regulations on energy companies and calls himself generally against regulation of business.

cut-welfare.rationale: Backs cutting mandatory spending but protects Social Security; no stated view on welfare creating dependency.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Sued five cities and Dallas over marijuana non-enforcement policies, saying the drug is linked to psychosis.

limit-guns.rationale: Sued over the ATF private-sale and stabilizing-brace rules as Second Amendment violations and campaigns to protect gun rights.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Prosecuting pimping under existing law is nearby; no stated position on legalizing consensual sex work.

decide-locally.rationale: Champions the Tenth Amendment and states over Washington, but sues Texas cities to override local policy on marijuana, sanctuary, gun and tax rules.

traditional-family.rationale: Coauthored the 2005 marriage amendment, said Texas defines marriage as one man and one woman, and campaigns on parental rights.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Coauthored the 2005 marriage amendment, backed clerks who refused licenses after Obergefell and fought same-sex licenses from "activist judges".

abortion-legal.rationale: Celebrated the end of Roe, calling it illegitimate, closed his offices in memorial, and pursues out-of-state abortion pill providers.

more-religion-public.rationale: Directed schools to display the Ten Commandments, urged students to recite the Lord's Prayer and said the nation was founded on Biblical truth.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Declared state diversity and race-conscious programs unconstitutional and said people should be judged on merit; says slavery was "fixed".

gender-social-construct.rationale: Calls transgender identification "transgenderism", misgendered a federal official, and mocks the idea of "six sexes".

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Says "we don't want to become Western Europe", vows to fight Sharia law, and frames his data-center plan as protecting Texas culture and land.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Sued repeatedly to end deportation freezes, DACA and parole programs, backs mass deportation and a border wall, while saying he wants legal immigration chosen by Congress.

free-trade.rationale: Backs tariffs but no stated view that free trade benefits everyone.

nation-first.rationale: Campaign states an "America First" approach to foreign policy and says Texas and America come first.

open-borders.rationale: Sued Biden over lifting border barriers and deportation freezes and backs border wall, deportation and ending sanctuary policies.

limit-growth.rationale: Campaigns on growth, jobs and lower energy costs by removing regulations and has sued over climate rules.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Sued to block Obama and Biden climate and emissions rules and backed ExxonMobil as defending a view in an "issue of scientific debate".

tax-inheritance.rationale: Attacked his opponent for voting for a "death tax" in Texas and framed it as something Texas does not need.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Told the Houston Chronicle in April 2025 he fully supports Trump tariffs because countries are coming to the table; campaign lists revitalizing American manufacturing.

separate-church-state.rationale: Directed Ten Commandments in classrooms and said nation was founded on the rock of Biblical Truth, rejecting a strict wall of separation.

military-superiority.rationale: A peace-through-strength slogan is nearby; no stated position on superiority over rivals.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Declared "equity" programs unlawful and said policy should reward merit, not outcomes by group.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Standing with Israel as a democracy is nearby; no stated position on a Jewish state in the Land of Israel.

school-vouchers.rationale: Issued the 2023 opinion clearing education savings accounts including for religious schools, and celebrated the universal school choice law, promising to defend it.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Says spending "like crazy" will bankrupt the country, wants to cut spending and the national debt, and promised to reduce the debt in his campaign.

force-without-un.rationale: Backs Trump on Iran; no stated position on UN approval.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Led a 14-state defense of the public-charge rule over Medicaid costs of illegal immigration and ended in-state tuition for undocumented students as benefits "not available to American citizens".

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Sued over EPA power plan and oil-and-gas rules, sued BlackRock over coal, and promises more oil and gas production.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Campaigns to "drain the swamp" in Washington and says Cornyn tends to side with the swamp and does what Karl Rove tells him.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Invokes judging people by character and not skin colour and says racial discrimination is wrong, but backs laws and actions that treat gay and transgender people differently.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Instructed schools to post the Ten Commandments and backed prayer and Bible displays in schools.

separated-powers.rationale: Said on air that the founders wanted three branches precisely because they did not trust people in power, and says he wants oversight of himself.

death-penalty.rationale: Took over the Robert Roberson capital case, insisted the sentence be carried out and requested an execution date.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Sued the Pornhub operator under the age-verification law, saying Texas has a right to protect children from pornographic content.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Called birthright citizenship a "scam that threatens national security" while suing a birth tourism centre.

ban-cartels.rationale: Said "I am totally free market" but that one firm controlling 97% of ad markets is why antitrust laws exist and asked for Google to divest; sued BlackRock, State Street and Vanguard as a coal "cartel".

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: His opinion declared mandates to consider race and sex for seats on state boards and commissions unconstitutional.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Issued an opinion that DEI and race-based preferences in government are unconstitutional and joined suits and letters against private DEI.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Says private employers face liability under state and federal discrimination law for DEI preferences and calls racial discrimination illegal.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Enforces a ban on land purchases by entities tied to China, Russia, Iran and North Korea; this does not address all foreigners.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said Big Tech firms "buy their way out of everything" and that Congress is hard to move because corporations give so much money.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Says transparency is what is needed in government, but his office has kept records such as animal research logs closed.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Said in 2022 he would defend sodomy laws if Lawrence were overturned; that is a statement as the state's lawyer, not a personal position, so no answer.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Sued doctors, hospitals, WPATH and the federal government over gender transition care and gender-identity rules and called "transgenderism" a cancer.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Attacks his opponent for wanting to "get rid of prisons" and for hostility to law enforcement.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Launched an investigation into noncitizens who voted, saying foreign nationals must not influence Texas elections.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Mocked a rival over "six sexes" and treats sex as fixed in suits over gender transition and sports.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Sued to block the EPA methane fee on oil and gas, calling it a tax that is "bad policy" as well as unlawful.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Joined briefs against Biden student loan cancellation, calling it an unlawful "wealth transfer" onto taxpayers.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Said it has been his "common refrain" that compulsory union dues are incompatible with individual liberty, endorsed paycheck-protection legislation.

voter-id.rationale: Cosponsored the 2011 voter ID law, defended mail-ballot ID rules and campaigns for the SAVE America Act requiring proof of citizenship and photo ID.

close-ties-china.rationale: Sued a Houston birth tourism centre aimed at Chinese nationals, is writing rules to enforce limits on land purchases by China-linked buyers, and pledges to ban Chinese technology and beat the Chinese Communist Party in AI.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Supports repeal of the federal gas tax according to press coverage; no stated position on consumption taxes generally.

notes: Attorney general suits count only where Paxton personally announced or championed them. Same-sex sodomy law remarks (2022) and defense of state laws as state lawyer were not counted. Tariff and Iran-war support come from press summaries. His mixed record on Big Tech/antitrust versus deregulation leaves regulate-corporations at 0.
